chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'If a person in ihram kills game,' he said, 'Upon him is the ransom.' I said: 'And if he repeats it?' He said, 'Upon him, every time he repeats it, is a ransom.'

key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةُ: Ransom or expiation (compensation for a religious violation)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: A person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim in ihram who kills game?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the principle of individual liability for each instance of game killing by a muhrim, a key point in Shia fiqh regarding whether the penalty is cumulative or fixed. It underscores the seriousness of violating the sanctity of the Haram boundaries, linking the physical act to spiritual accountability. The ruling reflects the broader Quranic emphasis on maintaining the integrity of pilgrimage rites.
